source.title: Pretraining a Neural Network before Knowing Its Architecture

record.tranche_reason: Compares initialization methods and reports their fine-tuning convergence on two architectures, conceptually testing whether initialization affects training speed. It does not test most of the claim versions’ specific settings or mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates fine-tuning on CIFAR-10 with 1,000 labels, not training from random initialization on the full CIFAR benchmarks. Table 1 reports test accuracy, not training classification error. Figure 4 shows training-accuracy curves; the text describes convergence speed but gives no numerical curve values. Cited findings are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates learned initialization and its post-processing for transfer learning in ResNet-50 and ConvNeXt. It reports its method's convergence and generalization performance, but does not test V4's activation-matched signal/gradient preservation in plain networks, depth dependence, or specified orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison. The other versions are also untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors find GHN initialization less useful for ConvNeXt than ResNet-50, suggest architecture distribution shift as a possible explanation, and identify highly correlated predicted parameters. Their noise-plus-orthogonalization post-processing improves test accuracy for both architectures, with a convergence benefit reported only for ResNet-50.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a trained Graph HyperNetwork to predict initialization parameters, then fine-tunes on reduced CIFAR-10; also evaluates conditional noise and orthogonal re-initialization. This is not the random-initialization classification-error recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence benefit of GHN-orth differs by architecture: present for ResNet-50 and not significant for ConvNeXt. ImageNet-pretrained models converge rapidly on both.

fits_no_version.finding: GHN-orth accelerates ResNet-50 convergence, but provides no significant convergence benefit for ConvNeXt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-processing GHN-predicted parameters can accelerate fine-tuning, with benefits depending on architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: ImageNet-pretrained models reach strong performance within 10–20 epochs under separately tuned training recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ImageNet pretraining enables rapid transfer learning on CIFAR-10 with 1,000 labels for ResNet-50 and ConvNeXt.

fits_no_version.finding: GHN-orth raises test accuracy from 61.8±0.3 to 65.6±0.2 for ResNet-50 and from 52.3±0.5 to 53.6±0.4 for ConvNeXt; ImageNet pretraining achieves 88.7±0.2 and 95.6±0.1, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-processing predicted parameters improves few-label transfer accuracy over GHN alone, while remaining substantially below architecture-specific ImageNet pretraining.

record.peer_reviewed: First Workshop of Pre-training: Perspectives, Pitfalls, and Paths Forward at ICML 2022, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: Results concern fine-tuning on CIFAR-10 with 1,000 labels rather than training error on the full benchmark. Training-accuracy curves are figure-only without numerical values. Only two architectures are evaluated; experiments use five seeds, with mean and standard deviation reported for test accuracy.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error from random initialization on the specified CIFAR benchmarks, including corrupted labels and recipe or model-size dependence.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.

Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients in plain networks; trainable depth; matched-variance orthogonal versus Gaussian weights in deep tanh networks; and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence.
Controlled comparisons of batch normalization and its absence, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the stated claim versions; this does not negate the reported method-performance findings. Figure 4's curve coordinates cannot be recovered from the supplied text. Generic evidence that starting parameters affect convergence is insufficient to test V4's more specific claim.

versions.untested_parts: Training error from random initialization; full CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model size, training duration, and regularization effects on training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Depth comparisons with and without identity shortcuts, and the stated plain-network or normalization conditions.

The paper compares initialization methods’ fine-tuning convergence, but does not test activation-matched signal/gradient preservation, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization at matched variance in deep tanh networks, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature changes, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization versus no normalization as a cause of faster training or higher learning-rate tolerance; Fixup.
